catalog_citation: Ali, Mukhtar Wakil, Ahmed Abbas Natilly, Hissein Gadim & Hashim [Aheel]. 1998. Cwaya Phonology. Revised by Elizabeth Guest, 28/3/98. Unpublished native-speaker orthography-workshop write-up, 9 pp. (scan formerly at rogerblench.info/Language/Niger-Congo/Kordofanian/Cwaya/, read from the Internet Archive copy; = PHOIBLE inventory 1499 source 'Ali 1998').
catalog_locator: Sec. IV 'Tone', p. 7 (first paragraph and example list), and sec. VI 'Orthography', p. 9 (closing paragraph plus handwritten note). Scan has; pp. 7-9 read
catalog_quote: IV. Tone [handwritten: Needs more investigation] There is evidence that tone is important in this language. There are two level tones and a falling tone. Below are listed words with lexical tone, and it should be noted that reading is considered very difficult when the tones are unmarked. In addition, direction is indicated by tone such that low-high indicates direction away from the speaker while low-low is direction towards the speaker. There are also instances of grammatical tone. [handwritten: eg pronouns] Away (L-H) àpá 'take' èlá 'go' Toward (L-L) àpà 'bring' èlà 'come' ... [p. 9] Tone will be written. Low tone will be unmarked since it is the commonly occuring tone. High tone will be marked with an acute (á). Length in both consonants and vowels will be indicated by doubling the letter as in gínná 'three' and caan 'follow'. [handwritten: also falling tone with ^]
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: Shwai/Cwaya is described as a tone language with two level tones (H, L) and a falling tone, carrying lexical and grammatical contrasts; the description says nothing at all about word stress or accent, so no stress position can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None (no stress discussion). Tone examples: àpá 'take' (away, L-H) vs àpà 'bring' (toward, L-L); làmà 'chin' vs lámà 'pot'.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms from native-speaker workshop data (area near Kadugli, c. 10,000 speakers per the ms); orthography-oriented write-up, explicitly flagged 'needs more investigation' for tone.
new_statements.identity_note: The 1998 ms calls the language 'Cwaya' / 'Shwaya' (same language as Glottolog shwa1239 Shwai, ISO shw; PHOIBLE files it under shw). Data from native speakers of the area 'near Kadoogali'; dialect (Shirumba/Cerumba vs Shabun vs Ndano) not stated. Schadeberg 1981's notes are on Shirumba proper (speaker from the Shirumba community recorded in Heiban).
